Question: Should the US and NATO be worried about the growing relationship between Russia and North Korea?
Answer: The relationship, no. The USSR and its successor state Russia have always had a relationship with the DPRK. Russia has always guaranteed the security of the DPRK because they would not want a South Korea or any western military force to occupy parts of the Korean Peninsula north of the 38th Parallel and closer to its border. They did not permit it in the Korean War and they won’t permit it now. The Putin visit to the DPRK was more in propaganda and show than a real policy change. Russia has carried on the USSR guaranteed defense of the DPRK. They didn’t need to pretend to sign documents, smiles and handshakes to reach that understanding thru Putin’s visit to Pyongyang. The real worry here is what weapons and technology upgrades Russia will supply to the DPRK. It appears China has the same concerns - even though they too would rather have a DPRK on the other side of the Yalu than South Korea with US troops. Modern technology in the hands of an unstable Kim is a concern for both his friends and enemies.
